newsitem.title: INDIA: India's RBI sets up forex technical advisory panel.
newsitem.headline: India's RBI sets up forex technical advisory panel.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on Tuesday said it set up a Forex Market Technical Advisory Committee to advise the central bank on policy issues.
"The committee will also advise the RBI on issues relating to risk management," it said in a statement.
R.V.Gupta, deputy governor in charge of exchange control, will be the chairman of the committee, RBI said.

It named the following members: B.K.Pal, RBI executive director, B.Y.Olkar of the Foreign Exchange Dealers Association of India, M.G.Bhide of the State Bank of India, Girija Pande of ANZ Grindlays Bank, Shailendra Bhandari of HDFC Bank, Narayan Seshadri of consulting firm Arthur Andersen, S.A. Kamath of the Bank of Maharashtra and S.Nandi of the National Institute of Bank Management.
Khizer Ahmed of RBI's exchange control department and Usha Thorat of RBI's department of external investments and operations will be the other members, the statement said.
The committee's terms of reference are:
+ To discuss technical issues referred to it by RBI and make recommendations to standardise practices for use in the market.
+ To prepare issue papers on specific market-related subjects, particularly on new products introduced in overseas markets.
+ To review the quality of risk management and the accounting and disclosure standards followed by banks and companies and suggest improvements.
The statement did not say when the new committee will start functioning.
